source: critique of /read-cua-docs.json (.agi/context/local-maxxing/troves/2026-09-19-cua/read-cua-docs.json, 20056 bytes, mtime 2026-09-18 20:22:43 EDT; keys = source/summary/key_facts[21]/reusable_assets/failures_and_lessons/hypothesis_seeds[4]/open_questions). Reviewer re-opened 7 cited sources on 2026-09-18: https://cua.ai/cuabench/leaderboard ; https://cua.ai/cuabench/report ; https://cua.ai/docs/concepts/what-is-computer-use ; https://cua.ai/docs/reference/cua-driver/mcp-tools ; https://cua.ai/docs/reference/cua-driver/mcp-tool-notes ; https://cua.ai/docs/how-to-guides/driver/connect-your-agent ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/cua-bench/cua_bench/agents/base.py . Also read the two LOCAL measured artifacts the reading ignored: .agi/context/local-maxxing/cua/cua_trace_excerpt.json and cua_trajectory_mapping.md (both mtime 2026-09-18 19:28:46 EDT, ~54 min BEFORE the reading was written). Verdict up front: the quoted numbers are almost all verbatim-correct, but the reading conflates two different trajectory formats, overstates the cheapness of its best reuse path, never flags two official-page contradictions, and ignores on-box evidence that already answers its own open question #1.
unsupported_claims: SEED 1 CONFLATES TWO LAYERS. It claims a Cua-Bench run 'exports one trajectory whose `turn-00001/action.json` carries typed action records (tool name, args, result, observation)'. `turn-NNNNN/action.json` is the Cua DRIVER recording format (start_recording; https://cua.ai/docs/reference/cua-driver/mcp-tools, fetched 2026-09-18) — it belongs to the driver layer, NOT Cua-Bench. Cua-Bench emits an HF dataset of events, MEASURED locally in cua_trace_excerpt.json: dataset_features = [event_name, data_json, data_images, trajectory_id, timestamp], events = reset / step:before / step:after / evaluate. There is no turn-NNNNN folder in a Cua-Bench trace. The seed's stated success criterion is therefore wrong for the tool it names.

SEED 2'S '<=20-line adapter' IS CONTRADICTED BY THE LOCAL MEASURED MAPPING. cua_trajectory_mapping.md (measured, 2026-09-18) maps cua->jev field by field and names 5 hard gaps: `model` has NO counterpart (traces are model-blind), and `http_status` / `input_tokens` / `latency_s` have no counterpart; `target` is pixel coords with no semantic selector/role/name; `act` identity is per-run not per-step. It states plainly: 'Mapping cua -> jev therefore costs a model call.' A <=20-line adapter is an ESTIMATE the reading presents as a plan without evidence; the on-box measurement says the mapping is lossy and non-trivial.

PLATFORM SCOPE UNFLAGGED. The reading's 56-tool count, action-tool list, and envelope facts are quoted from https://cua.ai/docs/reference/cua-driver/mcp-tools, which is titled 'MCP Tools (macOS)' and opens 'This reference describes the macOS native tool registry. Other platforms: Linux MCP tools...'. The town's box is ARM Linux. macOS-only surface (bundle_id/urls launch identifiers, TCC check_permissions.prompt) and Windows-only surface (debug_window_info) do not transfer; the Linux page is a separate document the reading never opens. The cross-platform envelope itself IS verified (mcp-tool-notes, fetched 2026-09-18: {path, verified, effect, escalation}, path rungs include x11_atspi/x11_pixel/msaa), so the envelope claim survives — but the reading never says it read the macOS page.

STEP-BUDGET NUMBER QUOTED WITHOUT FLAGGING THE OFFICIAL CONTRADICTION. The reading says '200-step budget' (leaderboard) in summary and key_facts. The report (https://cua.ai/cuabench/report, fetched 2026-09-18) says 'The point was to make the 150-step budget genuinely generous' and 'Every full pass finished under 150 turns'. 200 vs 150 is an unresolved discrepancy between two official pages; the reading reproduces 200 and never notes 150.

COHORT SIZE UNRECONCILED. The leaderboard lists 10 models; the report TL;DR says 'ran seven frontier computer-use agents' and names seven (GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 4.8, Gemini 3 Flash). Rank-1 Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol and Muse Spark 1.1 appear on the leaderboard but not in the report cohort. The reading reproduces both without noting they disagree.

COHORT-GENERAL VS SINGLE-RUN. The reading states 'self-verification is brittle -- Five of the nine runs that emitted DONE failed verification' as a general lesson. The report says the deep dive 'is drawn from an earlier Sonnet run that recorded four full passes; the leaderboard above reflects a later run at five' — the 5-of-9 figure is the Claude Sonnet 4.5 analysis, not the whole cohort. Generalizing it to all models is an overreach (the report does claim the failure modes 'recur across the other models', but the 5/9 count itself is Sonnet-only).

LICENSE ONE-SIDEDNESS. The reading repeats 'MIT-licensed framework' (true for cua-bench) but omits that the raw README lists third-party components under other licenses (OmniParser CC-BY-4.0; optional cua-agent[omni] pulls ultralytics AGPL-3.0) — already flagged in critique-cua-readme.json. For a 'reusable assets' trove this omission understates a real reuse constraint.

SEED 3's '$0; ~30-60 min' IS IN TENSION WITH THE READING'S OWN FAILURE NOTE. failures_and_lessons correctly records that 'Sandbox local mode depends on Docker/Lume/QEMU/Hyper-V; a 4-core ARM box without a VM/Docker path may be unable to run native providers at all.' The KiCad EDA suite is a native-provider (real OS/KiCad GUI) workload, not a simulated-Playwright one. The seed therefore proposes a $0 CPU run on a workload the reading itself says may be unrunnable on this box, with no reconciliation.
errors_found: MISSED LOCAL MEASURED ARTIFACT (the most consequential omission). .agi/context/local-maxxing/cua/cua_trace_excerpt.json and cua_trajectory_mapping.md existed at 19:28:46 EDT; the reading was written at 20:22:43 EDT — 54 minutes later. The artifact is a real cua-bench v0.2.11 simulated 'first-task' oracle run on ARM4C headless with reward 1.0. It directly answers the reading's open question #1 ('Does cua-bench's simulated (Playwright) provider run on aarch64 ARM with no VM/Docker?') and supersedes seeds 1 and 2. Unlike the sibling critique-cua-readme.json (whose reading predated the artifact), this reading had no timing excuse.

SEED 1's SUCCESS CRITERION IS A FORMAT ERROR. See unsupported_claims #1: `turn-NNNNN/action.json` is Cua Driver recording, not Cua-Bench. The local trace shows Cua-Bench's actual schema (event_name/data_json/data_images/trajectory_id/timestamp). A reader who grepped the repo before writing would have caught this.
200-vs-150 STEP BUDGET UNFLAGGED (leaderboard vs report). The reading quotes 200 and never notes the report's 150.
10-vs-7 COHORT UNFLAGGED (leaderboard vs report). The reading lists 10 leaderboard rows and never notes the report's seven-model cohort or that Claude Fable 5 is absent from it.
REPORT DEEP-DIVE SCOPE NOT STATED. 'Five of the nine DONE-emitting runs' and the four-full-pass table are from the Sonnet 4.5 run; the reading presents them as cohort-wide.
SEED 3 INTERNAL CONTRADICTION. The seed prices a KiCad single-edit run at $0/30-60 min while failures_and_lessons says native providers may be unavailable on this box. Both cannot be true as written.

NO VERSION/COMMIT PINNING. Every GitHub/docs URL is live 'main' or unpinned. The sibling critique already demonstrated main-vs-v0.2.11 drift (event names 'agent_step' vs 'step:before/after'; 4 vs 5 dataset fields). This reading repeats unpinned trajectory-format claims without an archive citation.

GOOD, for fairness: the numbers it did quote are almost all verbatim-correct. Re-verified 2026-09-18: leaderboard 10/10 rows (Claude Fable 5 6/25,2/25,0.267 ... Gemini 3 Flash 1/25,7/25,0.200); report 'Build-from-scratch tasks completed at 0/16', root cause '40% planning/policy, 22% perception, 19% navigation inefficiency, 11% domain knowledge, 8% tool-API', 'zero API errors', 467/488 steps, LT3010 V_REF 0.808V, '2.8k' vs '2.80kOhm', task 84ec333e 50 turns reward 1.0; base.py AgentResult(total_input_tokens,total_output_tokens,failure_mode) + FailureMode(unset/none/unknown/max_steps_exceeded/api_error); mcp-tools '56 MCP tools'; connect-your-agent 'Cua Driver 0.28.0 and later supports the MCP 2026-07-28 revision ... legacy clients ... 2025-06-18'. These check out.
missing_angles: The reading never looks in its own repo. The local measured run (cua_trace_excerpt.json + cua_trajectory_mapping.md) already proves the simulated provider works headless on ARM4C at reward 1.0, and already quantifies the cua->jev gaps. Any plan built on seeds 1/2 should start from that artifact, not from zero.

No aarch64/ARM feasibility check for the Cua DRIVER binary itself. The driver docs are macOS-first (the cited tools page is macOS) and the install path is not verified to ship an arm64 Linux build. This matters more than the benchmark for the town's box.

No per-task wall time, disk footprint, or RAM headroom for `cua-bench[browser]` + Playwright/Chromium on a 4-core ARM box with ~7 GB free. The reading gives effort estimates but zero local cost numbers.
No generalization caveat: the leaderboard/report is a single-domain (EDA/KiCad), v1-only suite. 'Best agent 6/25' bounds KiCad editing, not computer use broadly.

No mention that no open-weight model appears in the v1 EDA cohort — directly relevant to the owner's 'open model beats closed' premise (the sibling read-cua-readme reading is where this premise lives).
No check of whether the Cua-Bench evaluator/reward can run as a fully local $0 RL signal (listed as open question but not investigated from the repo, where the answer likely lives).
No license-component angle (OmniParser CC-BY-4.0, ultralytics AGPL-3.0) despite 'reusable_assets' framing.
No reconciliation of the report's two budget stories (150-turn design budget, 500-step extension, leaderboard 200) into a single 'what budget should a tiny-model experiment declare' recommendation.

No consideration that Cua Driver's per-action `verified`/`effect` are ACTION-level, while the report's dominant failure is ARTIFACT-level self-verification (netlist/title bar). The two are not the same signal; seed 4 assumes they are.
strongest_seed: Seed 2 (Cua-Bench trajectory -> jev typed-acts mapping), on the literal criterion of knowledge-per-token on CPU: it is pure-Python/JSON, $0, needs no VM, and is already half-measured locally (cua_trajectory_mapping.md). The reusable output — a typed-action corpus from a verifiable computer-use environment — is the cheapest durable knowledge asset on the list. BUT it must be reframed: the reading's '<=20-line adapter' is falsified by the local mapping, which found 5 gaps (no model field, no token/latency/http accounting, no semantic target, per-run not per-step act id). The honest seed is 'quantify and bound the lossy fields, then decide whether the mapped corpus is worth a model call', not 'write a trivial adapter'. Seed 3 is the highest-value-if-feasible seed (it tests the town's core thesis with a verifiable reward), but it is blocked by the native-provider/KiCad requirement the reading itself documents; seed 1 is already answered locally; seed 4 is weakest.
weakest_seed: Seed 4 (Cua Driver's per-action envelope {path, verified, effect, escalation} is a sufficient verification vocabulary for a tiny agent, addressing the report's dominant self-verification failure). Two independent reasons: (1) category error — `verified`/`effect` are per-action delivery/read-back signals ('the click landed'), whereas the report's failure is task-level artifact verification ('the saved netlist is correct'); the report says agents 'checked their own narration instead of reading the artifact', which a per-action envelope does not fix; (2) platform dependence — the cited page is the macOS registry, the reading never confirms an arm64 Linux driver binary exists, and the falsifier ('run cua-driver call get_desktop_state') silently assumes it does. It is also the least connected to the town's CPU-only, benchmark-scoring aim: the driver is the automation layer, not the evaluation or training signal.
